William Mark Price was born on February 15, 1964.
William Mark Price is an American former basketball player and coach.
William Mark Price was most recently the head coach of the Charlotte 49ers.
William Mark Price played for 12 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) from 1986 to 1998.
William Mark Price spent the majority of his career with the Cleveland Cavaliers.
William Mark Price's last three years consisted of one season each with the Washington Bullets, Golden State Warriors, and Orlando Magic.
William Mark Price stood at 6 feet (183 cm) tall.
William Mark Price played college basketball at Georgia Tech.
William Mark Price was a three-time All American during his time playing for Georgia Tech.
William Mark Price was a four-time All ACC basketball player during his time playing for Georgia Tech.
William Mark Price helped lead the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets to an ACC Championship his junior year by defeating North Carolina in the ACC Tournament championship game.
William Mark Price was named the ACC Player of the Year for the 1984–85 season.
William Mark Price's jersey was retired at Georgia Tech.
William Mark Price was inducted into the school's Hall of Fame in 1991.
William Mark Price was inducted into the Georgia Sports Hall of Fame in 2005.
William Mark Price graduated from Georgia Tech in four years with a degree in Industrial Management.
William Mark Price was selected first in the second round (25th overall) by the Dallas Mavericks in the 1986 NBA draft.
William Mark Price was acquired by the Cleveland Cavaliers in a draft day trade that helped turn the team into an Eastern Conference powerhouse.
William Mark Price finished his career with a 90.4% free throw shooting percentage and a 40% three-point field goal shooting percentage.

William Mark Price became the second player, after Larry Bird, to join the NBA's 50–40–90 club for those who shot at least 40% from three-point range, at least 50% from the field, and at least 90% from the free throw line in a single season during the 1988–89 season.
William Mark Price ranked consistently among the assist leaders.
William Mark Price twice won the Three Point Contest (in 1993 and 1994).
William Mark Price was named to the All-NBA First Team after the 1992–93 season.
William Mark Price was second in franchise steals with 734, a Cavaliers record that stood until December 9, 2008, when LeBron James surpassed him.
William Mark Price mystified critics who said he was too slow, too small and too deliberate for a high-level game.
William Mark Price was known as one of the league's most consistent shooters.
William Mark Price was plagued by injuries late in his career.
William Mark Price played one season for Washington Bullets before moving on to the Golden State Warriors.
William Mark Price signed with the Golden State Warriors as a free agent in July 1996.
William Mark Price played 70 games for Golden State and averaged 11.3 points per game during his time there.
William Mark Price was traded to the Orlando Magic for David Vaughn III and Brian Shaw on October 28, 1997.
William Mark Price spent one season with the Orlando Magic before being waived on June 30, 1998.
William Mark Price represented the United States national team during his career.
William Mark Price played in the 1983 Pan American Games where the team won gold medals.
William Mark Price also represented the national team in the 1994 FIBA World Championship, known as Dream Team II, and won gold medals.
William Mark Price's number, 25, was retired by the Cleveland Cavaliers not long after his retirement.
William Mark Price is a member of the Georgia, Ohio, and Oklahoma Sports Halls of Fame.
The city of Enid, Oklahoma, renamed the basketball arena Mark Price Arena as a tribute to his accomplishments since he was one of the best basketball athletes in Enid High School history.
Denny Price, William's father, was a successful player at Oklahoma and for the Phillips 66ers before becoming a college coach for Sam Houston State and Phillips University.
Brent Price, William's younger brother, played ten seasons in the NBA.
Caroline Price, William's daughter, had a short stint in professional tennis after playing for the North Carolina Tar Heels.
Josh Price, William's son, plays college basketball for Trevecca (2021-2022) after attending and playing two years for Liberty Flames.
William Price is a Christian and attends church.
Mark Price began his coaching career during the 1998–99 basketball season as a community coach under head coach and friend Joe Marelle at Duluth High School for the varsity boys team.

After discovering he had non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, Joe Marelle, Mark Price became a primary factor in the team's return trip to the final four of the class 5A GHSA state tournament. It was the first time Duluth High School returned to this point in the state tournament in 16 years.
Mark Price went on to be an assistant coach to Bobby Cremins at Georgia Tech during the 1999–2000 season.

After Cremins retired from coaching at Georgia Tech, Mark Price then went on the following year to be the head coach at Whitefield Academy in Atlanta for the 2000–01 season leading the team to a 27–5 record and the final eight teams of the state Class A tournament, a 20 win improvement over the prior season and 27 win improvement two seasons before Price arrived.
NBA player Josh Smith also played at Whitefield Academy the same season Mark Price was coach.
In 2002, Mark Price won the Coach Wooden "Keys to Life" Award.
In 2003, Mark Price was a consultant for the NBA's Denver Nuggets.
Mark Price then became an NBA television analyst and color commentator for both the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Atlanta Hawks.
In March 2006, Mark Price was named the inaugural head coach of the Australian NBL's South Dragons, a new franchise for the 2006–07 season.
Despite featuring NBL Rookie of the Year Joe Ingles and four time Olympian Shane Heal, the South Dragons began the season 0-5 and Mark Price was fired.
Mark Price and Shane Heal exchanged criticisms in the Australian press after Heal was named as his successor.
In December 2011, Mark Price was hired as a player development coach for the Orlando Magic.
In July 2012, Mark Price served as the head coach of the Orlando Magic's Summer League team.
On July 1, 2013, Mark Price was hired as an assistant coach by the Charlotte Bobcats, joining the staff of head coach Steve Clifford and associate head coach Patrick Ewing for the 2013–14 season.
On March 25, 2015, Mark Price was introduced as the head coach of the Charlotte 49ers. He replaced Coach Alan Major, who parted ways with Charlotte after two medical leaves during the past season.
On December 14, 2017, it was announced that Mark Price was relieved of his duties as head coach of the Charlotte 49ers basketball program.
In September 2018, he joined the Denver Nuggets coaching staff as a shooting consultant for the 2018-19 season.
